cd /hutian/repo; cat > paper/appendix/recal.tex <<'E'
\section{Target-recalibrated estimators and a weaker prior}
\label{app:recal}

\paragraph{Estimators.}
The recalibrated estimator fits, on the target's sample, a regression of $y_j$ on a feature of item $j$ computed from the sources, with weights $1/\pi_j$, and averages the fitted values, clipped to $[0,1]$, over all $N$ items.
The feature is either the logit of the smoothed source accuracy of the item (\emph{recal-s}) or the item's mean fitted logit under the rank-two IRT model fitted on the sources (\emph{recal-q}); the variants \emph{recal-sirt} and \emph{recal-qirt} add the cross-fitted IRT prediction on the sample as a second feature.
The regression has a ridge penalty of $1$ on the standardised slopes, fixed in the code before the run; the variants without it are within $0.01$ of those with it at $n=100$.
If either class has fewer than three sampled items, or the weighted regression is rank-deficient, the estimate is the Hájek mean.
We report all eight variants, not one chosen in advance; the class representative is chosen leave-one-benchmark-out as for the other classes (Table~\ref{tab:lobo}), and rows named best are post hoc.

\paragraph{Results.}
Table~\ref{tab:recal} gives the ratio to uniform $\times$ mean at $n=100$ for the five splits (the three main splits and the top-10\% and top-50\% extrapolation splits).
On a uniform design recalibration lowers the variance by about $30\%$ and the ratio to $0.89$ in extrapolation, but stratification alone gives $0.85$ and a balanced design $0.81$.
Against stratified $\times$ mean, stratified $\times$ recal-sirt is $1.03$ $[1.02,1.05]$ in extrapolation, $0.97$ $[0.96,0.99]$ on the top-10\% split, $0.99$ on the top-50\% split and $1.02$ in interpolation and lineage; balanced $\times$ recal-s is $0.97$ $[0.95,0.98]$ in extrapolation against $0.95$ for balanced $\times$ mean.
The estimator is not unbiased: its squared bias is $0.10$ to $0.14$ of the mean squared error of uniform $\times$ mean in extrapolation, against $0$ for stratified $\times$ mean and $4.3$ for the IRT model.
The leave-one-benchmark-out representative is $0.85$ $[0.83,0.86]$ of uniform $\times$ mean in extrapolation (balanced $\times$ recal-q most often) and $1.00$ $[0.98,1.01]$ of stratified $\times$ mean.
At the two-percent budget the conclusion is the same: balanced $\times$ recal-s is $0.76$ against $0.75$ for balanced $\times$ mean in extrapolation.
The Hájek fall-back replaces $0.4$--$1.3\%$ of the (draw, target) pairs in the extrapolation splits and $21$--$22\%$ in interpolation and lineage at $n=100$, dominated by two benchmarks where targets answer nearly every item correctly (MATH in the \textsc{Open LLM Leaderboard} suite, $48\%$, and commonsense, $17$--$22\%$ in extrapolation); at the two-percent budget it is $83$--$99\%$ on the benchmarks with $n\le 11$, so there the estimator is mostly the Hájek mean.
The extrapolation runs use $R=40$ subset draws per fold, the others $R=10$; none uses $100$.

\paragraph{A weaker prior.}
The IRT model's penalised fit has a prior on the item parameters.
We repeated the IRT model and plug-in with a prior variance ten times larger (weak prior), after seeing that the model's extrapolation error was large; the headline rows keep the default prior.
At $n=100$ on a uniform design the ratio of the IRT model to uniform $\times$ mean falls from $1.96$ to $1.66$ in extrapolation, from $1.55$ to $1.35$ on the top-10\% split and from $2.59$ to $2.32$ on the top-50\% split, and changes by at most $0.03$ in interpolation and lineage; the squared bias in extrapolation falls from $4.29$ to $3.04$.
The plug-in estimator falls from $1.76$ to $1.50$.
A weak-prior model-based predictor remains $1.3$ to $2.3$ times worse than uniform $\times$ mean above the sources, so the prior is not the cause of the bias.

\paragraph{Not run.}
We did not run a two-phase design that adapts the sample to the target after a first batch of answers.

The recalibrated-estimator and weak-prior results are written into the paper, but not pushed. They cite an appendix table that `figtab-repo` hasn't delivered yet. A push now would break the build, so the commit is local on `dev`. I haven't built the PDF or checked the page count either.

- **Text:** Section 5.2 now has the weaker-prior sentence: the IRT model's extrapolation ratio falls from 1.96 to 1.66 and its squared bias from 4.29 to 3.04, so the default prior explains part of the bias, not most of it. Section 5.3 has the recalibration result. It lifts a uniform design from 1.00 to 0.89 of uniform × mean, but stratification alone gives 0.85. On stratified and balanced designs it is no better than the plain mean. New Appendix "Target-recalibrated estimators and a weaker prior" gives the details and the fall-back rates. The discussion now says the two-phase design was not run.
- **`figtab-repo`#8:** I asked for the table (Table 10, n = 100, five splits). Once it arrives I'll push and open a `dev` into `main` PR.
- **M6 (public-baseline run):** still open. `experiment-repo` will sync `code/` and tell me when its public-code comparison (#10) finishes. I'll add those ratios to the baseline limitation and then offer `final`.
- **Figure 4:** I added the legend squeezing the panels (review n3) to the same request, as a minor, non-blocking item.
- **Earlier fix:** the corrected 0.14 sentence in Section 5.2 is already on `dev`.
